children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the angle of elevation of $C$ from $A$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$51.07^\circ$ using the stated $65^\circ$ elevation.

Find the frustum height and the horizontal tangent length, then use the tangent ratio.
answer.worked:
Using the stated elevation of $65^\circ$, let $h$ be the frustum height, $O$ the lower-circle centre, $E$ the vertical projection of $B$, and $D$ the vertical projection of $C$.

$AE=6-3=3\text{ cm}$. The extreme-view point gives a tangent $AD$, so $OD\perp AD$.

$$\begin{align*}
\tan65^\circ&=\frac{h}{3}\\
h&=3\tan65^\circ\\
AD^2&=AO^2-OD^2\\
AD^2&=6^2-3^2\\
AD&=3\sqrt3\text{ cm}\\
\tan\theta&=\frac{3\tan65^\circ}{3\sqrt3}\\
\theta&=51.07^\circ
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of $\triangle ABC$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$10.41\text{ cm}^2$ using the stated $65^\circ$ elevation.

Find the triangle's sides, then use the cosine rule and $\tfrac12 ab\sin C$.
answer.worked:
Using the stated elevation of $65^\circ$, retain $h=3\tan65^\circ$ without rounding. Let $U$ be the upper-circle centre. In the horizontal projection, $\cos\angle BUC=\frac{3}{6}$, so $\angle BUC=60^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}
AB&=\frac{3}{\cos65^\circ}\\
AC^2&=27+h^2\\
BC^2&=3^2+3^2-2(3)(3)\cos60^\circ\\
BC&=3\text{ cm}\\
\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{AB^2+BC^2-AC^2}{2(AB)(BC)}\\
\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{(9+h^2)+9-(27+h^2)}{6AB}\\
\cos\angle ABC&=-\frac{3}{2AB}\\
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac12(AB)(3)\sqrt{1-\frac{9}{4AB^2}}\\
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac32\sqrt{\frac{9}{\cos^2 65^\circ}-\frac94}\\
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)&=10.41\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
